subject: Urgent: AtlasCorp API throttle event — recovery plan & timeline
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@atlascorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasCorp Ops <ops+api@atlascorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:03Z
Subject: Re: AtlasCorp API — sudden throttling seen since 08:45

Marcus —

We started seeing sustained 429s across our ingest pipeline beginning ~08:45 UTC. The jobs that normally run at 08:30 started failing with: "rate_limit_exceeded: 429". This has blocked multiple critical data batches.

What changed on your side? Our traffic pattern hasn’t increased significantly. Can you confirm whether you rolled out a change to per-tenant caps or quota rules overnight? We attached a short log sample.

Attachment: throttle_sample.log (text/plain, 95KB)

We need either immediate mitigation or a rollback — our SLA-critical flows are impacted. Please advise ETA.

— Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, AtlasCorp

Lena —

Thanks for the quick report and the log. We’re investigating now. A few immediate notes and actions:

1) Can you confirm the tenant id / key in the log (we have a few aliases)?
2) I’ve asked SRE (cc’d) to throttle-bypass your tenant while they root-cause — that should restore flows within minutes.
3) I’ll follow up with a plan and timeline for permanent remediation and a formal postmortem.

We treat 429 production impacts as high priority — I’ll update you within 30 minutes.

Regards,
Marcus Lin

Date: 2026-10-28T09:33:45Z
Subject: Internal: initial triage — AtlasCorp 429 spike

Marcus / Neha —

Quick findings from the first pass:

- Root cause appears to be a policy mapping regression introduced in the per-tenant rate-cap rollout (v2.3) that deployed early this morning. A default mapping rule incorrectly mapped several tenants (including atlascorp-prod) to the stricter "baseline-safety" policy instead of their configured committed tier.
- The rollout change set: infra/ratecaps/20261027-apply.json shows a missing override key for "tenant_aliases". That allowed the default to match broader tenant groups.
- Action taken: I applied a temporary bypass for tenant id "atlascorp-prod" at 09:39Z to allow traffic while we prepare a safe rollback. Bypass will remain until 10:00Z unless you request longer.
- Next steps: rollback the v2.3 mapping and then re-apply with a corrected override and an explicit tenant whitelist. Estimated time for rollback test and deploy: ~20–30 minutes.

I’ve attached the audit output and the mapping diff for reference.

Attachment: policy-audit.log (text/plain)

Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-28T09:45:00Z
Subject: AtlasCorp throttling — mitigation applied and next steps

Lena / AtlasCorp team —

Update and immediate remediation:

• At 09:39Z we applied a temporary bypass for tenant "atlascorp-prod" which restored your ingest jobs. Please confirm if your backfills are progressing.
• Root cause: a mapping regression in the per-tenant rate-cap v2.3 rollout mapped your tenant to a stricter baseline policy. SRE has staged a rollback of the mapping and will re-deploy with the corrected override.
• Timeline: rollback verification and safe redeploy targeted by 10:15Z; full revert and monitoring until 10:45Z.
• Customer-facing artifacts: I’m attaching a short remediation plan that outlines the rollback, validation steps, and our offer for SLA credit if the incident caused downstream failures. We will deliver a formal postmortem within 72 hours.

Attachments: atlas_remediation_plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Related: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-10-28-atlas-throttle (live updates)

If you want us to keep the bypass in place longer while you run longer backfills, tell me the window and we’ll extend it.

Sorry for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the full root cause, timeline of code/config changes, and concrete remediation actions.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Enterprise accounts
Redwood Inference
